title: Mukhyamantri Lakhpati Didi Yojana Uttarakhand 2026
meta_description: Mukhyamantri Lakhpati Didi Yojana Uttarakhand makes SHG women earn Rs 1 lakh+ per year through livelihood support. Eligibility, how to join, and benefits.

hero.one_liner: Mukhyamantri Lakhpati Didi Yojana helps Uttarakhand SHG women earn at least Rs 1 lakh a year through interest-free loans, skill training, and market support.

what_is_it: Mukhyamantri Lakhpati Didi Yojana is the Uttarakhand government's flagship initiative to transform women in Self Help Groups (SHGs) into 'lakhpati' (earning Rs 1 lakh or more annually) through a structured combination of skill training, livelihood promotion, enterprise development, and market access support. The scheme targets SHG members across both rural and hill areas of Uttarakhand, aiming to lift women's household incomes sustainably and permanently above the Rs 1 lakh annual threshold through multi-source livelihood strengthening rather than one-time transfers.

The scheme is a state-level complement to the national PM Lakhpati Didi Yojana announced by the central government. While the central scheme sets a nationwide target of creating 3 crore lakhpati didis across India, the Uttarakhand state government's version specifically addresses the unique challenges faced by hill-area SHG women, including geographic isolation, limited market access, seasonal income constraints, and reliance on subsistence agriculture.

how_to_apply.title: Join an active SHG
how_to_apply.description: Enroll in a registered and active Self Help Group in your village under the USLM or NRLM framework. The SHG must maintain regular savings, timely loan repayment, and monthly meetings to qualify as active for the Lakhpati Didi Yojana.

how_to_apply.title: Baseline income assessment
how_to_apply.description: The USLM field team conducts a baseline assessment of your current income from all sources (dairy, farming, handicrafts, wages). This baseline is used to identify which livelihood streams need strengthening and what support (training, credit, market linkage) is needed to reach Rs 1 lakh.

how_to_apply.title: Receive skill training and inputs
how_to_apply.description: Based on the livelihood plan, receive targeted skill training from Krishi Sakhi, Pashu Sakhi, or USLM resource persons. Access improved seeds, animal breeds, or equipment through the scheme's input support or bank credit, and link to the relevant government scheme benefits.

how_to_apply.title: Link to markets
how_to_apply.description: The USLM Block Programme Manager connects your SHG cluster to bulk buyers, aggregation centres, or digital platforms for selling products. This market linkage ensures you receive remunerative prices for your produce rather than selling at distress prices to local traders.

how_to_apply.title: Income reassessment and certification
how_to_apply.description: After 12 months or as determined by USLM, a participatory income reassessment is conducted by the SHG, the Village Organisation (VO), and the USLM field team. If your income has crossed Rs 1 lakh annually, you are certified as a 'Lakhpati Didi' and entered into the state portal.

how_to_apply.title: Become a peer resource person
how_to_apply.description: Certified lakhpati didis are enrolled as peer resource persons to support other SHG women in their cluster. You receive recognition from the district administration, may be invited to state-level events, and continue to access market linkage support for maintaining and growing your income beyond Rs 1 lakh.

extra_sections.heading: Lakhpati Didi Yojana: The Basics
content: Uttarakhand has a strong SHG ecosystem built over decades through the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) and the Uttarakhand State Livelihood Mission (USLM). The Lakhpati Didi Yojana leverages this existing network by targeting SHG members who are already part of an active group and providing them with the training, resources, and market connections needed to cross the Rs 1 lakh annual income threshold.

Eligibility for the Mukhyamantri Lakhpati Didi Yojana is linked to SHG membership. A woman must be an active member of a registered SHG in Uttarakhand under the USLM or NRLM framework, with the group maintaining regular savings, timely loan repayments, and monthly meetings as the basic threshold of an 'active' SHG qualifying for scheme benefits.

extra_sections.heading: Lakhpati Didi Yojana: The Basics: in Practice
content: The income target of Rs 1 lakh per year per woman is achieved through a multi-source livelihood portfolio. For a typical hill-area SHG woman in Uttarakhand, the sources of income that together build to Rs 1 lakh might include dairy and animal husbandry income, earnings from agro-processing enterprises (like fruit processing, pickling, herbal products), income from handloom and handicrafts, homestay tourism earnings, and any wages from MGNREGA or other government work programs.

The skill training component of the Lakhpati Didi Yojana covers both production skills (how to improve quality and quantity of existing livelihood activities) and entrepreneurship skills (how to price, market, and sell products). Training is delivered through USLM's network of resource persons, Krishi Sakhi, Pashu Sakhi, and other community resource persons who are themselves skilled SHG women trained to transfer skills to their peers.

extra_sections.heading: The Numbers That Matter
content: Market linkages are a critical component of the scheme, addressing the core reason SHG women in hill areas earn below Rs 1 lakh despite their productive activity: the inability to access remunerative markets for their products. The Lakhpati Didi Yojana connects SHG clusters to buyers through the Uttarakhand Organic Commodity Board, the USLM marketing platform, GEMs and Amazon Saheli e-commerce, and state-level fairs and exhibitions.

The scheme also focuses on reducing input costs for SHG women, as in hill agriculture the cost of seeds, organic fertilisers, and packaging can significantly eat into enterprise margins. By aggregating procurement through SHG clusters and Cluster Level Federations (CLFs), the Lakhpati Didi Yojana enables bulk purchasing that reduces per-unit costs and improves the net income retained by each woman member.

extra_sections.title: Start With a Realistic Activity
extra_sections.content:
Pick an activity you can actually run with the resources and time you have, like dairy, pickle making, or tailoring.

A steady, smaller enterprise that you sustain beats an ambitious one you cannot maintain. The mission staff can help you choose.

extra_sections.heading: The Numbers That Matter: Further Notes
content: Animal husbandry is one of the most significant livelihood streams for hill-area women in Uttarakhand, and the Lakhpati Didi Yojana gives particular attention to improving dairy income. SHG women are supported to access improved breed cattle through the Rashtriya Gokul Mission, receive training from Pashu Sakhis on animal care and fodder management, and connect with dairy cooperatives or local milk collection centres to ensure they receive fair prices for their milk production.

Homestay tourism is another emerging livelihood stream promoted under the Lakhpati Didi Yojana for SHG women in Uttarakhand's tourist destination areas such as Mussoorie, Nainital, Rishikesh, Kedarnath pilgrimage belt, and Kumaon hill resorts. Women who own or operate homestays can earn significantly from tourist accommodation and meals, and the scheme provides training in hospitality management, hygiene standards, and digital booking platforms to help SHG-linked women enter this sector.

extra_sections.heading: Who Is Eligible
content: The Uttarakhand government has set specific targets under the Lakhpati Didi Yojana for the number of women to be made lakhpati each year, with district-wise targets assigned to the USLM district programme managers. Progress is tracked through a monitoring dashboard that records each SHG woman's baseline income, the interventions she receives, and her income reassessed after intervention to confirm whether she has crossed the Rs 1 lakh threshold.

Women who have already crossed Rs 1 lakh in annual income and are certified as 'lakhpati didis' become part of a peer learning network under the scheme. They serve as role models and resource persons for other SHG women working toward the threshold, demonstrating achievability from local livelihood activities; this peer learning model is central to scaling the scheme efficiently across Uttarakhand's dispersed hill geography.

extra_sections.title: The Yearly Income Target
extra_sections.desc:
The name Lakhpati Didi comes from the goal of helping each woman earn at least Rs 1 lakh a year.

This is sustained income from her own work, not a one-time grant, so the benefit continues year after year.

extra_sections.heading: Who Is Eligible: in Practice
content: Financial inclusion is a foundational component of the Lakhpati Didi Yojana; SHG women must have Aadhaar-linked bank accounts for government payments, subsidies, and credit flows that support livelihood activities. The USLM works with banks and Business Correspondents (Bank Mitras) to ensure SHG women in remote hill villages can access credit through SHG lending, Mudra loans, and other formal financial products.

The convergence with other central and state schemes is a key design principle: handicraft makers access the SFURTI cluster programme; food processors link to PM-FME; farmers access PM-KISAN; dairy women link to dairy infrastructure schemes. The Lakhpati Didi Yojana acts as an umbrella framework that actively channels eligible SHG women into these other scheme benefits rather than operating as a standalone programme.

extra_sections.heading: Getting Your Application In
content: The scheme has a specific focus on Uttarakhand's tribal and marginalised communities in both the Garhwal and Kumaon divisions. SHG women from SC, ST, and OBC categories are prioritised in outreach, training, and market linkage support; the USLM district teams must ensure lakhpati didi certification targets include proportional representation from these communities.

Monitoring of income progress under the Lakhpati Didi Yojana is based on participatory income verification conducted through the SHG group, the CLF, and the USLM district team. Rather than requiring documentary income proof (which is difficult to produce for informal rural livelihoods), the scheme uses community-verified income assessments that cross-check the woman's livelihood activities, sales records where available, and group knowledge of her income sources.

extra_sections.title: An Income Scheme, Not a Cash Handout
extra_sections.content:
Lakhpati Didi does not pay women a monthly amount. Instead it helps a woman earn at least Rs 1 lakh a year through her own enterprise.

It works through Self-Help Groups, giving interest-free loans, skill training, and market links so members build a lasting income.

extra_sections.heading: Getting Your Application In: More Detail
content: Women who become lakhpati didis under this scheme gain not only income but also a significant improvement in social standing within their households and communities. The recognition that a woman is earning Rs 1 lakh or more annually through her own enterprise or livelihood work shifts the household's economic dynamic, strengthens her voice in family decisions, and often motivates other women in her SHG or village to intensify their own livelihood activities.

The Uttarakhand government's Mukhyamantri Lakhpati Didi Yojana is complemented at the national level by the PM Lakhpati Didi Yojana, which provides additional resources through the Ministry of Rural Development and NRLM. Uttarakhand's state budget allocation for the scheme supplements the central resources, enabling the state to run additional training programmes, provide higher-quality market linkages, and cover more SHG women than would be possible with central resources alone.

extra_sections.heading: The Fine Print on Eligibility
content: The long-term vision of the Mukhyamantri Lakhpati Didi Yojana is to create a cadre of economically self-reliant women leaders in every village of Uttarakhand. When a woman earns Rs 1 lakh or more annually, her family's nutritional security, children's education, healthcare access, and housing conditions all improve measurably; by multiplying such women through the SHG network, the scheme works as a force multiplier for rural poverty reduction across the hill state.

SHG women interested in benefiting from the Mukhyamantri Lakhpati Didi Yojana should approach their village-level SHG, the Village Organisation (VO), or the Block Programme Manager of USLM in their area. The USLM portal at uslm.uk.gov.in provides information on the scheme, district-level contacts, and the ongoing training programmes available for SHG members at any given point in the calendar year.

extra_sections.heading: The Fine Print on Eligibility: Further Notes
content: The role of the SHG cluster and the Cluster Level Federation (CLF) extends beyond individual women; at the cluster level, SHGs pool their products for bulk processing and sale, share equipment like processing machines or packaging units, and jointly access loans for capital investment. This collective action model reduces the infrastructure cost per woman while allowing each member to benefit from the scale advantages that individual production alone cannot achieve.

The Uttarakhand state government coordinates the Lakhpati Didi Yojana with the Department of Agriculture, the Animal Husbandry Department, the Horticulture Department, and the Tourism Department to ensure that technical support and scheme benefits from each department are channelled efficiently to SHG women working in those sectors. This inter-departmental coordination is essential because the income streams that contribute to the Rs 1 lakh target typically span more than one department's jurisdiction.

extra_sections.title: Not a Monthly Payment Scheme
extra_sections.content:
Do not expect a fixed monthly amount in your account under this scheme. That is a different kind of welfare programme.

Lakhpati Didi is about building your own earning, so the real benefit is the income your enterprise generates over time.

extra_sections.heading: Your Document Checklist
content: The promotion of natural farming and organic produce under the Lakhpati Didi Yojana aligns with Uttarakhand's positioning as a state committed to organic agriculture. SHG women who produce organic grains, Himalayan herbs, and traditional vegetable varieties can command premium prices through the Uttarakhand Organic Commodity Board's platform and from health-conscious urban buyers, making organic cultivation one of the higher-margin livelihood options promoted under the scheme.

Digital literacy is an increasingly important component of the Lakhpati Didi Yojana, as many of the market linkage opportunities (GEMs portal, Amazon Saheli, online booking for homestays) require basic smartphone and internet skills. The USLM includes digital literacy modules in its training programmes, and SHG women who complete digital training are better positioned to independently manage their online sales, check government scheme portal status, track their income digitally, and communicate directly with buyers in distant urban markets without depending on intermediaries who previously captured much of the price margin.

extra_sections.title: Your Document Checklist Notes
extra_sections.content:
The scheme's emphasis on documentation and record-keeping among SHG women has a secondary benefit of improving financial management habits. When SHG members are required to maintain simple income records for the participatory income verification process, many women begin tracking their income and expenses more carefully, which leads to better decisions about credit, investment, and saving within the household and the SHG group.

Uttarakhand's geography means that many SHG women operate in areas with limited connectivity, infrequent market access, and seasonal road blockages due to snow or landslides. The Lakhpati Didi Yojana accounts for these constraints by promoting livelihood activities with long shelf life and low perishability (dried herbs, woollen handicrafts, processed foods) so that production can happen throughout the year even when market access is seasonal.

extra_sections.heading: The Bigger Picture
content: The scheme's convergence with the PM-FME (Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food Enterprises) scheme is particularly valuable for SHG women in agro-processing. PM-FME provides capital subsidy of up to Rs 10 lakh for food processing enterprises, and SHG women in the Lakhpati Didi Yojana who qualify can access this subsidy to purchase equipment that raises their production capacity and quality, directly contributing to higher annual income from their enterprise.

The Lakhpati Didi Yojana represents a shift in how Uttarakhand approaches women's economic empowerment: from viewing SHG women as beneficiaries of welfare schemes to recognising them as potential rural entrepreneurs and skilled producers. The Rs 1 lakh income target, modest as it may seem in urban terms, represents a genuine economic transformation for a hill-area woman whose household may previously have survived on less than half that amount annually, and for whom crossing this threshold means fundamentally improved household dignity, food security, and decision-making power within the family.

extra_sections.title: The Bigger Picture More Notes
extra_sections.content:
For Uttarakhand's hill economy, the multiplication of lakhpati didis within SHG networks has a broader macroeconomic significance. When large numbers of women in a district consistently earn Rs 1 lakh or more per year, local demand increases, children's nutrition and school attendance improves, and household vulnerability to economic shocks from natural disasters or crop failures reduces; the scheme thus operates as both a livelihood intervention and a structural resilience measure for Uttarakhand's hill communities.

The administrative tracking of lakhpati didi progress at the district and block level in Uttarakhand also helps the state government identify which livelihood streams are most scalable and which areas face the greatest barriers to income growth. This data, aggregated through the USLM monitoring system, informs future budget allocations, training programme priorities, and targeted infrastructure investments to maximise the number of SHG women successfully crossing the Rs 1 lakh threshold each year across all 13 districts of Uttarakhand, including the remote and high-altitude ones.

extra_sections.heading: Some Added Notes
content: Recognising that Uttarakhand's tourism economy is a significant opportunity for SHG women, the Lakhpati Didi Yojana has special provisions for women in pilgrimage circuit districts including Chamoli, Rudraprayag, and Uttarkashi. Women in these areas can link their food, accommodation, and handicraft production directly to the tourism value chain, earning from both domestic pilgrims visiting the Char Dham sites and adventure tourism visitors, making tourism-linked livelihoods one of the highest-potential pathways to lakhpati didi status in these districts.

faqs.question: What is Mukhyamantri Lakhpati Didi Yojana Uttarakhand?
faqs.answer: Mukhyamantri Lakhpati Didi Yojana is the Uttarakhand government's initiative to enable SHG (Self Help Group) women to earn Rs 1 lakh or more per year through skill training, livelihood promotion, and market linkage support. It complements the national PM Lakhpati Didi Yojana with state-specific programmes for hill-area SHG women.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for the Mukhyamantri Lakhpati Didi Yojana?
faqs.answer:
Active members of registered SHGs in Uttarakhand under the USLM or NRLM framework are eligible. The SHG must be actively functioning with regular savings, timely loan repayments, and monthly meetings.

There is no separate income limit for eligibility - women currently earning below Rs 1 lakh annually are the target group.

faqs.question: What is the Rs 1 lakh income target and how is it achieved?
faqs.answer: The Rs 1 lakh annual income target is achieved by combining and strengthening multiple livelihood streams: dairy and animal husbandry, agro-processing (fruits, herbs, pickles), handicrafts and handloom, homestay tourism (in tourist areas), and wage work including MGNREGA. The USLM provides training, credit access, and market linkages to strengthen each stream.

faqs.question: What training and support is provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer:
Skill training through USLM resource persons, Krishi Sakhis (for agriculture), and Pashu Sakhis (for animal husbandry). Market linkage through the Uttarakhand Organic Commodity Board, GEMs portal, Amazon Saheli, and state fairs.

Credit access through SHG bank linkage, Mudra loans, and NRLM revolving funds.

faqs.question: How is a woman certified as a Lakhpati Didi?
faqs.answer: Income is assessed through a participatory community process involving the SHG, the Village Organisation (VO), and the USLM field team rather than formal documentary proof. If the assessment confirms annual income of Rs 1 lakh or more from combined livelihood sources, the woman is certified as a Lakhpati Didi and entered into the state monitoring portal.

faqs.question: What happens after a woman becomes a Lakhpati Didi?
faqs.answer: Certified lakhpati didis become peer resource persons for other SHG women working toward the Rs 1 lakh target. They continue to access market linkage support and skill upgradation, receive recognition at district and state-level events, and are featured as role models in the USLM outreach programmes.

faqs.question: Is the Lakhpati Didi Yojana the same as PM Lakhpati Didi Yojana?
faqs.answer: No. PM Lakhpati Didi Yojana is the central government scheme under the Ministry of Rural Development with a national target of 3 crore lakhpati didis. Mukhyamantri Lakhpati Didi Yojana is Uttarakhand's state-level version that supplements the central scheme with state budget resources, addressing the specific challenges of hill-area SHG women in Uttarakhand.

faqs.question: How do I join the Mukhyamantri Lakhpati Didi Yojana?
faqs.answer:
Contact your village-level SHG, the Village Organisation (VO), or the Block Programme Manager (BPM) of USLM in your block. You can also check uslm.uk.gov.in for district contacts and training schedules.

The starting point is being a member of an active, USLM-registered SHG in Uttarakhand.

faqs.question: What livelihood activities are promoted under the scheme in hill areas?
faqs.answer: Dairy and animal husbandry (cow, goat milk), fruit and herb processing (himalayan herbs, apricots, apples), handloom and handicrafts (woollen products, ringal bamboo crafts), homestay tourism, organic farming with market linkage through the Uttarakhand Organic Commodity Board, and participation in MGNREGA for wage income during the non-crop season.

faqs.question: Where can I get more information about Lakhpati Didi Yojana in Uttarakhand?
faqs.answer: Visit the USLM portal at uslm.uk.gov.in, contact your district's USLM District Programme Manager, or approach the Block Programme Manager at the block development office. The village-level SHG and the VO (Village Organisation) can also provide guidance on enrollment and available training slots.
